record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Determine the smallest integer m for which there exists a planar polynomial differential system with exactly m monomials and at least m + 1 limit cycles.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. (ii) Find the minimal m such that there exists a planar polynomial diﬀerential system with m monomials having at least m+1 limit cycles: the simplest polynomial diﬀerential system with more limit cycles than monomials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polynomial differential systems of the form
  dx/dt = P(x,y),   dy/dt = Q(x,y),
where P, Q ∈ ℝ[x,y]. Define the number of monomials of such a system to be the total number of distinct monomials x^i y^j appearing with nonzero coefficient in P and Q combined (counted across the two components, so the same monomial appearing in both P and Q is counted twice). A limit cycle is an isolated periodic orbit of the system in the plane.

Determine the smallest positive integer m for which there exists a planar polynomial differential system with exactly m monomials (in the sense above) that possesses at least m + 1 limit cycles. Equivalently, find the simplest (in monomial count) planar polynomial differential system having strictly more limit cycles than monomials.
artifact.category_tag: planar polynomial vector fields and limit cycles
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of locating the minimal m such that some planar polynomial system with m monomials has at least m+1 limit cycles is part of an active research program proposing a monomial-count variant of Hilbert's 16th problem. Results exist showing that 3-monomial systems can attain arbitrarily many limit cycles, and explicit examples of systems with more limit cycles than monomials are known, but no proof of the actual minimal value of m has been established. The question is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles for 3-monomial differential equations
status_evidence.snippet: For planar polynomial differential equations ż = Az + Bz^k z̄^l + Cz^m z̄^n, there are equations of this type with at least p limit cycles for each p ∈ ℕ.
status_evidence.claim: 3-monomial planar systems can produce arbitrarily many limit cycles, far exceeding the number of monomials, but the minimal m attaining m+1 limit cycles remains undetermined.

status_evidence.title: Planar chemical reaction systems with algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit examples of planar polynomial systems with more limit cycles than monomials are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Examples exist of systems with more limit cycles than monomials, but the minimal monomial count m is not pinned down.
